title: The Rime of the Ancient Mariner
subtitle:
Forward with heads bowed
The ship drove fast, loud roared the blast,
The southward aye we fled.

trails.title: Ghost Story
trails.description: This comes from the personal experience of a radio enthusiast, there's no way it could be false.

content.text:
"So last night I picked up a really weird shortwave station."
"Was it a buzzer? Or a numbers station? Could just be interference."
"No, there was a woman's voice spelling letters, but it made no sense. MYDA, SEVA ... She also said something quite creepy."
"Did you record it?"
"Only got a few clips. Here, listen."

"Mike, Yankee, Delta, Alpha ... *static noise*"
"Sierra, Echo ... Victor, Abandon ... I'm the only one left ... Am I really the only one? No, I-I can't give up, no ... *static noise* Run away!"
"Mike ... Yankee, Delta, ugh, what? *static noise* Buzzing ... the bug is in my ears ... buzz ... Buzz, Bless ... Blasphemy! We brought on the devil's wrath! This is blasphemy!"​
"Starve,  I'm so hungry ... Is this thing edible?"
"I'm close to the *static noise* end now."
"A frozen corpse, a broken skull ... I must ... *static noise* ... find Mother Spirit ... guide ... *static noise*"
"..."
"Hotel, Lima, Evil ... Providence. The radio's not working, the radio ... I need to throw it away. Mother Spirit, bless me."

items.text: The Rime of the Ancient Mariner

items.speaker: Team Member I
items.text: Entering the ice zone. Grab your telescopes, explorers.

items.speaker: Team Member II
items.text: That's right. We need your eyes on every ice floe. Let's not make a second Titanic.

items.speaker: Team Member I
items.text: This isn't the time for jokes, Koht.

items.speaker: Nautika's Diary
items.text: Hearts thumping with excitement, our team set off. Thanks to our courage and careful preparation, it wasn't long until we crossed the Drake Passage.

items.speaker: Nautika's Diary
items.text: No matter how fierce the katabatic winds were, our will stood firm. In fact, the windstorm we met was very similar to the lab-simulated ones. It didn't take long for the captain to find a way to deal with it.

items.speaker: Nautika's Diary
items.text: Soon, we were sailing through the South Shetland Islands. There wasn't much there but black moraine and a few groups of Adélie penguins.

items.speaker: Nautika's Diary
items.text: It was clear to us that there was more trudging to be done before we reached our destination. But every one of us was confident that a journey of this magnitude would pay off with very many ancient secrets.

items.speaker: Nautika's Diary
items.text: When the sun dawned, we saw the lichen that grows all over the Aitcho Islands. Crimson, green, ocher ... Even the landblink couldn't pale those colors.

items.speaker: Nautika's Diary
items.text: That was when we realized that rocks can move too.

items.speaker: Nautika's Diary
items.text: I can't help but recall when the famous Guvernøren returned with a full and bountiful load. We celebrated the harvest very amazingly.

items.speaker: Nautika's Diary
items.text: We opened a keg of beer and sang the songs of home under the rosy sky.

items.speaker: Expedition Team Members
items.text: "The harvest's bounty mankind's blessing be. We children, blind, from mazes must be free."

items.speaker: Expedition Team Members
items.text: "The Mother Spirit's light, with ancient glow, guides us to the great current—nature's flow."

items.speaker: Nautika's Diary
items.text: Yes, we are the polar explorers. We are meant to be the challengers of the most unknown greatness.

items.speaker: Nautika's Diary
items.text: So, with this feeling in our hearts, we will continue our march into the depths of Antarctica.

items.speaker: Nautika's Diary
items.text: Carpe diem, as the saying goes. I've never felt more joyful and fulfilled and worthy in my entire life.
A two-stroke diesel engine sputters.
Bzz—bzzt— *thud* ...
Sparks fly as the radio transmitter groans.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: I, I must ... I must send it out.
A ragged, maddened voice comes from the research station's darkest corner,
speaking into broken equipment with undeliverable messages.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: *panting* Calm down, Nautika. Calm down.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: This is your research station. You built it together with the team.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: You're safe now. Yes, the Mother Spirit will protect you. You're ... You're safe now.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Just-Just try it one more time, just one more.
Her fingers keep pressing the broken transmitter key while her body shakes uncontrollably.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Come on, come on. You can do it. It's simple. You didn't go crazy. You have all your brains in here in your head. It knows all the letters of Morse code and how to send them.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: See? There's A, and D, and E, F, C. You know them all. Just use them to spell out the warning message and send it out across the whole world ... everyone. It, it's easy, like playing a game of "tablut." Yes, so easy.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: I can do this.
She munches down on a black gelatinous fluid in her mouth.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Cold. This moldy lime juice and disgusting ice algae, this damn frostbite ... Nothing left to do but sit here, stinking of blood, and wait for death to take me.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: I have to warn the world. This place isn't the last oasis, and there's no such thing as the Hollow Earth.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: But-But no one will believe me if they don't see it with their own eyes. Nobody!

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Because ...

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Because I used to be the same way.

items.speaker: Ear Worm Máhtu
items.text: "Through Giant Mother's bones the path is laid. In bloody pain, eternal life is made."

items.speaker: Ear Worm Máhtu
items.text: "The Mother Spirit's light, with ancient glow, guides us to the great current—nature's flow."

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Not now, little Máhtu.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Mother Spirit, bless me. Lend me your glorious strength and grant me your protection. L-Let me live through this.
"Boom—" A thunderous noise comes from outside.
The small figure startles.
She sidles to the window, peeking through the insulation's edge.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: A Snow Monster ship?
Excuse me, is anybody ...

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Please don't come over here, please, please, please.
A bright-haired "Snow Monster" has invaded the explorer's last refuge.
Excuse me, is there anyone here? We just landed, and this is the only building around. We were hoping to ask for some help.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: I-I'm already half frozen to death. Don't you dare crack my skull and suck my blood. I won't taste any good.
My apologies. There must have been some kind of misunderstanding.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Plague in the glacier, the worms beneath the feet of the Mother Spirit, and those sickening masked tyrants.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Bring it on, Snow Monster. If I can wrestle a reindeer, then I can take on you.
W-Wait!

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: You're not a Snow Monster?

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: N-Normal behavior, no mask, uses magic, yes, warm magic. I can move my fingers again.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text:
You're right, Máhtu. They don't seem like bad people. 
At least, not as bad as the Snow Monsters.
Crazed but still wary, she shrinks back to keep an eye on the intruders.
The two newcomers seem without concern. They straighten the furniture and examine the scene as if looking at a puzzle.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Hm. According to Mr. Aleph, this should be the coast that Dr. Dores landed on.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: This plain is the way to the heart of Antarctica. We may still catch up with her if we pick up our pace.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I see. But I didn't expect there to be a research station all the way out here.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: This place isn't on any map of Antarctica I've ever seen. It must have been built less than half a year ago.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: The facilities are quite complete. Diesel generators, snowmobiles, radio transmitters ...
Sonetto steps forward. An empty can rolls to her feet.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: However, they seem to have run out of food.
Her eyes turn to the cowering figure.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We're just passing by. We mean no harm. Is there anyone else at this station that can help us?
A hundred days of solitude ends with a simple question. Nautika stands half-hobbled in the corner, rubbing her nose.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: N-No. There's no one else.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Only me.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: I don't mean to offend, miss, but you don't look very well. May I give you a health evaluation?

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: No, no need. I'm fine. I'm an explorer. I-I know my body. I'm fine.
She retreats back from the newcomer's offered hand.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: What are you eating?
Nautika clutches black slime—a fibrous, mucus-like fluid oozing between her fingers.
She licks her lips and swallows it whole.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: The only thing there is to eat here.
Sonetto shakes her head.
And the suitcase's metal clasps are opened with two clicks.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Please, take this. It's turnip and potato soup with beef. I hope it suits your tastes.
Food.
Fresh food.
The long-suffering explorer reaches out as tenderly as a fawn.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: I-Is that a magic suitcase?
She points at the suitcase that conjured food out of thin air.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Yes. It's an arcane suitcase. It's bigger on the inside. It can hold food, rooms, even arcanists themselves.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: So you're arcanists!
Color finally returns to her pale face as she begins to examine her visitors with fresh eyes.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: That's right.
A protein-rich aroma wafts up from the tin.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Actually, we're heading to the heart of Antarctica. Perhaps you'd be willing to offer us some advice?
She knocks over the tin in panic. The soup inside splatters out across the floor.
Her body shakes erratically, and she returns to a mantra of bizarre muttered half-phrases rehearsed in her mind over and over again.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: No. You mustn't. Do not go into Antarctica.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: You mustn't go any further!
